scopeAccuracy.explanation: The delegation-credential validation path (validateToken -> findByPrefix -> hash verify -> revoked check) resolves principals per request through the credential-lookup pool BEFORE any tool runs; it is not executed inside the restricted workspace transaction. mcp_tokens RLS applies to allura_app; the gateway's credential-lookup role in production is the owner-backed pool. This proves revocation denial on a reused credential-validation pooled connection, not inside a restricted workspace transaction. The restricted read path for documents (proved pooled-revoked in the 2026-09-25 evidence) and this credential-validation path are distinct real paths; both are now timed-verified, on their respective real paths.
scopeAccuracy.transportSessionTeardownExplanation: The streamable-HTTP MCP gateway session lifecycle (mcp-session-id -> transport map) was not exercised; only the token validation path was tested.
scopeAccuracy.gatewayCredentialCacheExplanation: Correction recorded 2026-09-28. The canonical MCP HTTP gateway does not authenticate through validateToken; it uses HttpAuthenticator.authenticateMcpToken, which has a configurable non-device credential cache (ALLURA_MCP_AUTH_CACHE_TTL_MS, default 0, maximum 60000 ms) with a paired-device bypass. The credential minted here has no paired_device_id, so it is in the cacheable class. That path was NOT exercised: with a non-zero configured TTL, non-device revocation on the gateway may lag by up to the configured TTL. The earlier wording 'no authorization cache exists on the validation path' overstated the tested scope and has been narrowed.
